Q: Use Uri.encode implementation in Java library A:

You can convert the string before returning it:

return new StringBuilder(encodedString);

Or use StringBuilde.replace method (which is faster but you will only nothe the difference if you use it inside a wide loop):

StringBuilder encodedString = new StringBuilder();
encodedString = URLEncoder.encode(originalString, "UTF-8")
  .replace(0, originalString.length(), "\\+", "%20")
  .replace(0, originalString.length(), "\\%21", "!")
  .replace(0, originalString.length(), "\\%27", "'")
  .replace(0, originalString.length(), "\\%28", "(")
  .replace(0, originalString.length(), "\\%29", ")")
  .replace(0, originalString.length(), "\\%7E", "~");

Q: Separate my mainview into independent parts A:

Thank you :) This was exactly I was looking for.

During my research about the dos and don'ts working with UserControls I asking myself "Should a UserControl have its own ViewModel?" The answer is: It depends!

Also good to know for other Avalonia users who start working with UserControls: You have to reference the namespace of your Views inside the .axaml like so:

xmlns:local="clr-namespace:MyApp.Views"

After that you can use

<local:MyExtraView />

to insert a UserControl into a View like MainView. And yes it seems its a good practise to place your UserControls into the View folder / namespace.

Q: How to use update all, when all records are different? A:

Just stumbled across this, you can use upsert_all with options, in rails 7 and onwards: https://blog.kiprosh.com/rails-7-adds-new-options-to-upsert_all/

This ought to work:

Model.upsert_all(
   [
     { id: 22974, column: 2 },
     { id: 22975, column: 33 },
     { id: 22976, column: 94 },
     { id: 22977, column: 32 },
   ],
   update_only: [:column]
 )

It won't call ActiveRecord callbacks.
